data.title: A/B Test
data.tagline: An experiment that randomly assigns eligible users to variants and compares them using predefined metrics
data.learningOutcome: You can check whether an A/B test has a hypothesis, concurrent random assignment, predefined primary and guardrail metrics, and a stopping rule.
data.description: Eligible new visitors can be randomly shown one of two sign-up pages during the same period, then compared on completion rate. A before-and-after comparison or changing metrics mid-test does not provide the same causal evidence.

learning.assumes: You need to compare two options but may rely on before-and-after data, a few clicks, or personal preference.
learning.outcome: You can check whether an A/B test has a hypothesis, concurrent random assignment, predefined primary and guardrail metrics, and a stopping rule.

explanation.title: Answer one main question
explanation.text: Define the change and primary metric before running the experiment.

explanation.title: Randomize concurrently with matching definitions
explanation.text: Use the same eligible population, event definitions, and time window for both groups.

explanation.title: Predefine the decision and stopping rule
explanation.text: Set primary and guardrail metrics, sample needs, and stopping conditions before launch.

data.boundary: An A/B Test uses randomized comparison. A before-and-after report cannot remove other changes over time. A Feature Flag can control exposure, but exposure control alone is not an experiment.

lessonPractice.title: Which approach is closest to a valid A/B test for two sign-up guides?

options.label: During the same period, randomly assign eligible new visitors to A or B, predefine completion and error rates, and analyze after the agreed sample and duration
options.feedback: Correct. Concurrent random assignment reduces traffic and time differences, while predefined metrics and stopping rules limit result picking.

options.label: Show B to everyone this month and compare it with A from last month
options.feedback: Traffic sources, campaigns, and seasonality may change, so the difference cannot be attributed only to the page.

options.label: Check hourly and stop as soon as one version briefly leads
options.feedback: Short-term random variation can create a temporary lead. Set the analysis window and stopping rule before launch.

data.agentPrompt: Draft an A/B test plan for these two sign-up guides. State one hypothesis, eligibility, random assignment, the primary metric, guardrail metrics, analysis window, and stopping rule. Check that both groups use the same tracking definitions. Produce the plan and verification checklist only: do not start the experiment, change traffic, or call a temporary lead a winner. A data specialist should confirm the statistical decision.
